23.description: The committee recommends transferring $766,300 from city reserves to stabilize special event funding and proposes temporary changes to application intake for 2026-2027.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
City Manager strongly disagreed with Discover Saskatoon's competitiveness claims
Special event organizers and local community groups seeking funding.
Mayor Block questioned if fixed intakes would hurt event competitiveness.
Committee recommends an exception to policy for special event application intakes.
Discover Saskatoon supports stabilization but urges strategic, differentiated funding for events.
Administration promised a report by 2029 on long-term special event funding solutions.

19.description: The committee recommends developing a policy to guide how the city acquires and sells land for affordable housing. This aims to reduce costs for developers and ensure a stable supply of sites, especially for Indigenous-led projects.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 0 against
Mayor Block questioned the 20-year limit on affordable housing commitments.
Non-profit organizations could get flexible payment options for land.
This policy would replace the city's current ad hoc approach to land disposition.
The funding strategy for land acquisition is yet to be developed.
Métis Nation–Saskatchewan supports the policy for culturally relevant housing.
Policy introduces risks like reduced city revenue and high acquisition costs.
Administration will develop the formal policy and bring it back for approval.

chips.text: Recommended to Council

Efforts are underway to incorporate 57 black-owned startup businesses into the market.
